RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 10

That number is a subjective estimate, not a statistically grounded probability. An all-women panel is not, by itself, evidence of sex bias. You and the successful candidate are both women; nothing described establishes that sex influenced the outcome.

Your stronger question concerns how the published criteria were applied. A completed PhD, publications and teaching experience matter, but industry experience, interview performance and departmental needs may also carry weight.

Follow up now requesting the written reasons, selection criteria and any available scoring. Check review deadlines rather than waiting indefinitely. If a completed PhD was mandatory, specifically ask how that requirement was satisfied. Raise panel composition only if a relevant rule required a different composition.
